definition_title: Fixed-data interfaces for the determinant contradiction
natural_language_statement:
For a real approximation exponent $
u$, let fixed data be admissible parameters with the source arithmetic constant and collision constant $c=\log(2)/4$. Write $M(H)$ for the row count, $N(H)$ for the low-index count, and $b(H)$ for the normalized weighted row mean. Define the associated matrix, selected minor, and

$$\gamma(H)=\frac{c\eta^2M(H)}{H N(H)},\qquad \gamma_\infty=\frac{c\eta^2K\theta^m}{(m+1)v_0A^m}.$$

The global interpolation hypothesis asserts that, for every $
u>2$, every fixed datum and every real lower height, some larger height has a surjective matrix linear map. The analytic aggregate hypothesis asserts that every such datum admits an error tending to zero whose eventual determinant bound is the exact source analytic-and-collision estimate. These are the original quantified interfaces for the conditional determinant contradiction.
